overview: Diffusion is the spontaneous mixing of gas molecules throughout available space; effusion is the escape of gas molecules through a tiny pinhole into a vacuum or lower-pressure region — both follow Graham's law, but they describe different physical situations.
genZNote: Diffusion: gases mingling freely. Effusion: gas molecules sneaking out one tiny hole at a time.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Spontaneous mixing/spreading of gas molecules through another gas or space.
aspects.valueB: Escape of gas molecules through a small opening (pinhole) into a vacuum or region of lower pressure.

aspects.label: Requires a Tiny Opening?
aspects.valueA: No — occurs freely through available space.
aspects.valueB: Yes — specifically occurs through a small pinhole/orifice.

aspects.label: Governing Law
aspects.valueB: Graham's law of effusion (same mathematical form).
